answer: Each epoch the registry auctions only 100 identity slots. Applicants bid bonds on the canyon board, and the top 100 win; a jade receipt binds each slot to one key and cannot be transferred. The k-th fake identity costs at least the k-th highest honest bid, so 1,000 fake slots at a 40-credit clearing price lock 40,000 credits, and each extra slot pushes the price higher, not cheaper. A shale audit layer records every bid, so auditors can trace a rented-bid ring to one funder behind many keys and void all its slots. An honest applicant pays 40 credits once and keeps the slot.
